solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Enormous deficiency in fossil fuel

indicators.note: the shortfall word sits in the middle of the fuel word, split open around it

parts.note: coal is the classic fossil fuel
a deficiency is a loss or shortfall

explanation.surface: A worrying report of a huge shortage in fossil fuel supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of vast, gigantic size; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Plum variety

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, plum means excellent or select, as in a plum job
a range to pick from, as in a wide selection of goods

explanation.surface: A greengrocer naming a type of plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is a select one, and a wide variety offers plenty of selection: two senses of one word.

clue.text: Room in shelter on course

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next means it comes first

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a way is a route or course

explanation.surface: Finding room in a shelter along a route.
explanation.definitionFit: Room in the sense of scope or freedom to manoeuvre, a margin of latitude.

clue.text: Drink Japanese drink, around noon, before snack

indicators.note: the first assembled piece comes ahead of the snack word
the rice wine wraps around the single letter for midday

parts.note: a bite is a quick snack

explanation.surface: A bar order: rice wine around midday, then something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A snakebite is a British pub drink of lager mixed with cider.
explanation.definitionFit: The named drink is a mixture of lager and cider served in British pubs.

clue.text: Part of what is expected, and no trouble

definitions.meaning: something within one's normal duties, routine for the job
said of a task that is easy and causes no bother

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off a task as routine and easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means routine work within one's normal duties, so taking it in stride as no bother.

clue.text: Starts to realise he's yet to hear Mersey beat

indicators.note: the opening letter of each following word is taken, those words being the starts

explanation.surface: Someone realising they have yet to hear the Liverpool Merseybeat sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Merseybeat was the 1960s Liverpool pop sound, which makes 'beat' look part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat in music is the regular pulse or pattern of stresses, the same as tempo pattern.

clue.text: Problem struck church

explanation.surface: Trouble at a church that was struck, perhaps by lightning.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or difficulty, as in a plan going off without a single snag.

clue.text: That worm agitated pig

indicators.note: stirred up and disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A worm stirring up a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a British breed of ginger-coated pig, named after the Staffordshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional British breed of pig with reddish-gold bristles, so an example of the animal.

clue.text: Film politician almost embracing artist close to breakdown

indicators.note: the shortened politician word holds the next pieces inside it
the politician word loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: a member, as in Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A politician hugging an artist who is close to a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' points to cinema but means a thin layer; 'almost' leaves MEMBE, the politician word cut short, to do the embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin skin or layer, such as a film over a surface, is a synonym for this tissue.

clue.text: Sanctimonious author in hotel, getting drunk after hours

indicators.note: becoming tipsy and unsteady, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A smug writer getting drunk in a hotel after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' shuffles AUTHORINHOTEL together with H.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a self-righteous person who thinks they are morally superior to others.

clue.text: Protective garment in the past given to everyone

parts.note: over means finished, done with, in the past

explanation.surface: Protective clothing once handed out to all workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose garment worn over clothes to protect them from dirt, as in workwear.

clue.text: Plump single mother could be best

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it

explanation.surface: A chubby lone parent might turn out to be the best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb, as in plump for.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the most favourable or ideal, the very finest option.

clue.text: Follow lawsuit involving hospital

indicators.note: the lawsuit word takes in the hospital letter

explanation.surface: Pursuing a lawsuit that involves a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue or run after someone is to follow them.

clue.text: Happy hour binge in one next door

indicators.note: happy in the sense of merry or tipsy, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinking spree during happy hour, with the person who lives next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy hour' looks like a phrase, but 'Happy' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in the adjacent house is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: Infant school class painting in splotchy green

indicators.note: the painting word goes inside the rearranged colour
covered in blotches, so the colour's letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A class of young children painting in messy green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splotchy' gives ERGEN, and 'in' splits it after its third letter; 'class' here means type, not a school form.
explanation.definitionFit: A school for very young children before formal schooling, named from the German for children's garden.

clue.text: US prosecutor up, calling for confession

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mission is a vocation or calling

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor stands up demanding that someone confess.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgment of guilt or fault, just like owning up.

clue.text: Grub in new Norwich motel's original

indicators.note: made new, so the city's letters are put in a fresh order
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Food found in a new motel in Norwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Norwich is a city in eastern England; 'Grub' suggests food but means a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is a caterpillar or larva, and the looper caterpillar is one example.

clue.text: Talks foolishly about the Spanish members of the clergy

indicators.note: the talking word goes around the Spanish article

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length

explanation.surface: Gossip about Spanish priests.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelates are high-ranking churchmen such as bishops, senior clergy.

clue.text: Tender lines by Frost, say, in something read to a child?

indicators.note: next to, so the sound-alike piece follows the first part
said out loud, so the frost word gives a word of the same sound

explanation.surface: A gentle poem by Robert Frost that might be read to children.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Frost the poet is a red herring: 'Frost' is the ice, and 'say' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's verses like Humpty Dumpty are what parents read aloud at bedtime; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Hat wife discarded, plus old jacket

indicators.note: added on after, joining the next piece
the wife letter is thrown away from the hat

parts.note: a bowler is a hard round hat

explanation.surface: A hat thrown aside by a wife, along with an old jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket, as worn by Spanish dancers.

clue.text: Cupboard shut by last in basement

indicators.note: the final letter in the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A cupboard shut away in a basement.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage especially, a closet is a storage cupboard or wardrobe.

clue.text: Large market town, a Welsh one, misrepresented

indicators.note: presented wrongly, so the letters are given in another order

explanation.surface: A large market town wrongly claimed as Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Halesowen is a market town in the West Midlands of England, not in Wales, which fits 'misrepresented'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sizeable market town near Birmingham, an example of the category given.

clue.text: Poet's black fur

definitions.meaning: in poetry and heraldry, the dark colour of night
the pelt of a marten prized for its dark coat

explanation.surface: A poet's black fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means black in poetic use and is also the prized pelt of a small dark mammal.

clue.text: Winds back cylindrical device

indicators.note: the letters of the winding word are read backwards

parts.note: winds in the sense of loops, as with coils of string

explanation.surface: Something that winds back on a cylinder, like a reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel or bobbin on which thread or film is wound is a cylindrical device.

clue.text: Month round Connecticut — temperate, no sun

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut

indicators.note: the sun letter is removed from the temperate word

explanation.surface: A month around Connecticut, mild but without sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the tenth month of the year, an example of the category given.

clue.text: Someone having the potential to succeed

definitions.text: Someone having the potential to succeed

parts.words: Someone having the potential to succeed
parts.note: seems to mean a promising achiever, but succeed means inherit, as from a parent

explanation.surface: A description of a promising young achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter set to inherit a fortune stands to succeed to it, in the sense of take over.

clue.text: Fording Welsh river, came across an old firearm

indicators.note: the meeting word straddles the river, as one crossing it would

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Crossing a Welsh river, someone stumbled on an antique gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A musket is a muzzle-loading long gun of the era before rifles.

clue.text: Traitor's act shown on film

indicators.note: the act word goes on top of, so ahead of, the layer word

parts.note: a turn is an act in a variety show
a coat is a thin layer or film, as of paint

explanation.surface: A traitor's deeds are put on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests cinema but means a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who deserts their side for the enemy betrays it, just like a traitor.
